productDefinition.title: AI Software Engineer
productDefinition.originalText:
The problem i want to solve is not writing code. It is preventing software from being built incorrectly because of incomplete analysis, missing requirements, misunderstood business rules, or poor architecture — and then having to rebuild it from scratch.

### 1\. The Product We Want to Build

### AI Software Engineer

From an idea to an implementation-ready engineering package

Understand the Client

Even when they cannot articulate their idea

Analyze the Problem

Discover gaps and contradictions

Design the System

Data, processes, and relationships

Prepare for Implementation

Documents and testable tasks

Final deliverable

### Software Engineering Package

Approved requirements + architecture + database design + API contracts + UI specifications + implementation plan + tests

This platform does not need access to my existing projects or code repositories. It acts as a virtual software engineer who sits with a client, understands their needs, analyzes the system, and prepares the complete project specification from scratch.

### 2\. How Should the Virtual Software Engineer Work?

It must not treat the user as a programmer. It should treat them as someone who has a problem and wants a software solution.

Imagine a user says:

> I want an application that connects merchants with suppliers and helps merchants obtain the best prices.

This sentence is nowhere near sufficient to build an application. The virtual engineer must not immediately create database tables or choose Laravel, React, or another technology. It must first understand the actual business.

### 01

Understand the Problem and Objective

What problem does the merchant face today? How do they currently solve it? Who is affected? What outcome do they want to achieve?

### 02

Discover the Real Business Workflow

How does a merchant register? How do they find a supplier? How do they request a quotation? What happens if a supplier rejects the request, changes the price, or does not respond? Who makes each decision?

### 03

Discover Hidden Requirements

Ask about permissions, exceptions, notifications, payments, cancellations, errors, modifications, reporting, privacy, and other scenarios that users may not think to mention.

### 04

Transform the Understanding into a System

Define users and roles, inputs and outputs, processes, business rules, data entities, relationships, interfaces, and integrations.

### 05

Review and Approve the Analysis

Present the system understanding to the client in plain language. Let them correct misunderstandings and approve decisions before proceeding to the final design.

### 06

Deliver an Engineering Package

Convert the approved specifications into interconnected documents, dependency-ordered implementation tasks, acceptance criteria, and tests that demonstrate whether each task is complete.

### 3\. The Core Engines Inside the Platform

I recommend building specialized engines that work together through one unified workflow, rather than creating a collection of disconnected tools.

| Engine                                  | Primary responsibility                                                                                         | Output                                      |
| --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| 1. Idea Understanding Engine            | Understand natural language, including dialects, and translate it into precise Arabic and English descriptions | Unified problem and idea definition         |
| 2. Requirements Discovery Engine        | Conduct interactive interviews and identify missing information                                                | Approved requirements and decision register |
| 3. Business Process Analysis Engine     | Analyze workflows, inputs, outputs, states, and exceptions

discoverySummary.summaryMarkdown:
## Business problem
Software is often built incorrectly due to incomplete analysis, missing requirements, misunderstood business rules, or poor architecture, leading to costly rebuilds from scratch. All business outcomes are equally affected by incorrect software development.

## Target users
Primary decision-makers and influencers in the software development process at target companies are AI agents.

## Product format
Web application with responsive design.

## Business model
Freemium model with premium features.

## User journeys
Non-technical business stakeholders will interact with the platform through a hybrid approach: structured framework with conversational AI for exceptions.

## Scope
End-to-end specification generation with validation workflow.

## Constraints
Bootstrapped approach with flexible timeline, prioritizing revenue generation early.

## Success criteria
Technical performance metrics - accuracy of specifications generated, processing time, and system reliability.
openRisks: Unclear how primary decision-makers and influencers can be 'AI agents' in real business contexts
No specific details about which premium features will be included in the freemium model
No information about how the hybrid structured/conversational approach will be implemented
No technical details about the validation workflow

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: Data Protection
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The platform must protect all user data, including business problem statements and generated specifications, from unauthorized access, breaches, and misuse.
acceptanceCriteria: All user data must be encrypted both in transit (TLS 1.2+) and at rest (AES-256)
System must undergo annual penetration testing with a maximum of 2 critical vulnerabilities allowed

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: User Privacy
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The platform must ensure user privacy by collecting only necessary data and providing clear controls over personal information.
acceptanceCriteria: Platform must comply with GDPR and CCPA privacy regulations
Users must be able to delete their account and all associated data with a single request

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: Response Performance
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The platform must deliver fast and responsive interactions to maintain user engagement and productivity.
acceptanceCriteria: Average response time for business analysis and specification generation must be under 3 seconds for 95% of requests
Page load time for initial dashboard must be under 2 seconds on a standard broadband connection

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: Accessibility
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The platform must be accessible to users with diverse abilities and support multiple languages including Arabic with proper RTL rendering.
acceptanceCriteria: Platform must meet WCAG 2.1 AA accessibility standards
Arabic interface must display correctly with proper RTL text alignment and support for Arabic characters in all input fields and generated documents

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: Service Availability
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The platform must be consistently available to users, especially during business hours, to support their software engineering workflows.
acceptanceCriteria: Platform must maintain 99.5% uptime during core business hours (9 AM - 5 PM EST, Monday-Friday)
System must have automated failover capabilities with a recovery time objective (RTO) of under 15 minutes

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: Scalability
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The platform must scale to handle increasing user loads and growing project complexity without degradation in service quality.
acceptanceCriteria: System must support a minimum of 10,000 concurrent users without performance degradation
Architecture must allow horizontal scaling to handle 5x the expected peak load within 30 minutes

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: Maintainable Architecture
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The platform's codebase and architecture must be designed for long-term maintainability to support continuous improvement and feature additions.
acceptanceCriteria: Code must maintain a test coverage of at least 80% for all critical business logic
System must support zero-downtime deployments for non-critical updates

nonFunctionalRequirements.title: Intuitive User Experience
nonFunctionalRequirements.description: The platform must provide an intuitive interface that guides non-technical users through the software engineering process without requiring technical expertise.
acceptanceCriteria: Onboarding completion rate for new users must be above 70%
User satisfaction score (CSAT) for the specification generation workflow must be above 4.0 on a 5-point scale

risks.description: The platform handles sensitive business information but lacks explicit data encryption standards for both data at rest and in transit.
risks.mitigation: Implement AES-256 encryption for all stored data and TLS 1.3 for all data transmission, with mandatory key rotation every 90 days.

risks.description: User data collected during business analysis could be inadvertently used to train AI models without explicit user consent, violating privacy expectations.
risks.mitigation: Implement a clear privacy policy with opt-in consent for data usage in model training, and create strict data governance policies preventing unauthorized use.

risks.description: The hybrid approach of structured framework with conversational AI could lead to unpredictable response times, especially during peak usage.
risks.mitigation: Implement load testing with simulated user traffic and establish auto-scaling mechanisms for the conversational AI component based on predefined thresholds.

risks.description: The freemium model with premium features creates complexity in user management and access control that could lead to privilege escalation vulnerabilities.
risks.mitigation: Implement role-based access control (RBAC) with regular audits of user permissions, especially during subscription upgrades and downgrades.

risks.description: The bootstrapped approach with early revenue prioritization may lead to underinvestment in security infrastructure, creating long-term financial risk from potential breaches.
risks.mitigation: Allocate a minimum of 15% of development resources specifically to security testing and infrastructure hardening, regardless of revenue pressures.

risks.description: The unified workflow for specialized engines may become a bottleneck as user numbers grow, limiting the platform's ability to scale horizontally.
risks.mitigation: Design the workflow engine with a microservices architecture from the outset, allowing individual components to scale independently.

risks.description: The platform's success depends on specification accuracy, but there's no clear validation process beyond client approval buttons, potentially leading to undetected errors in critical specifications.
risks.mitigation: Implement a mandatory validation step where generated specifications are cross-checked against industry-standard templates before being presented to the user.

risks.description: Targeting AI agents as primary users creates uncertainty about adoption, as these agents may not have the authority to approve specifications or commit to subscriptions.
risks.mitigation: Develop a separate onboarding workflow specifically for AI agents that includes integration with existing enterprise systems and clear value propositions for human stakeholders.
